First run: 68 errors across all four files. Final run: exit 0, 0 errors.

The typecheck found a real latent defect, not just missing annotations. j1-linear.test.ts:185 read `late.error.code` on a `GoalReducerResult` union — `Property 'error' does not exist on type 'GoalAcceptedResult'`. `expect(late.ok).toBe(false)` on the line above is a runtime assertion vitest does not use to narrow, so had the reducer ever started ACCEPTING a post-cancel start — the precise regression that schedule exists to catch — the next line would have thrown TypeError on undefined rather than reporting a schedule failure. Same shape in j4 at three sites. Now routed through typed `accepted()`/`refused()` narrowers that throw a named error.

Harness typing, no `any` anywhere:
- `accepted`/`refused`: generic over `TResult extends OkOrRefused`, returning `Extract<TResult, {ok:true|false}>`, so the caller keeps its own core/contracts result type and `state`/`envelope`/`error.details` stay typed. Single narrowing cast each, after a runtime discriminant check.
- `fixturePayload(fixtureId, typedConstant)`: `FoundationFixture.payload` is `unknown` by design (one manifest, three journeys). Rather than cast, the caller passes the exported typed constant and this asserts referential identity with the registered fixture — the fixture stays the source of registration, the constant the source of the type, and a fixture rebuilt from different data throws.
- `produceAbsenceOutcome` / new `missingEvidenceOf`: reject an entry of the wrong outcome kind instead of falling back to a pass.
- `executorFor` replaces `EXECUTORS[entryId]`, which under noUncheckedIndexedAccess was `... | undefined`; a missing executor now throws a named ReferenceError rather than "not a function".
- `assertPartitionOwnership` no longer takes `expect` as an untyped parameter; the harness imports it.

Also caught by the stricter shapes: `decodeEnvelope({leaseAuthority:{epoch:7}})` could not be expressed once the override was typed, because a half-built lease authority is not a `FakeLeaseAuthority`. Rather than widen the fake's type (which would weaken every honest caller), the malformed case now builds the record explicitly through a `decodeRecord` seam. Same assertion, and the type now says out loud that the value is deliberately not a lease authority.

comments.content:
GOVERNOR NOTE for whoever claims this next — read before re-running anything.

QA's rejection is correct and the design is not the problem. Do NOT rewrite the specification; QA said so explicitly.

The defect is that this task's DECLARED verification command cannot reach its own owned paths:

  Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/testkit typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/testkit test
  resolves to:  vitest run --root ../.. packages/testkit/src

That glob matches packages/testkit/src only. It does not match tests/fault/foundation/**, which this task also owns. Three files — j1-linear.test.ts, j3-crash.test.ts, j4-replan-stale.test.ts, 43 tests — never executed in the evidence filed as exitCode 0. They pass when run directly. QA confirmed this by mutation, not by reading.

Second, related defect: no tsconfig in the repo includes tests/. packages/testkit/tsconfig.json is include ["src/**/*.ts"] and there is no root tsconfig covering tests/. So tests/fault/foundation/** is neither typechecked nor run by the declared gate.

This is not something a worker can fix by trying harder. Re-running the same command will produce the same false green. You have two legitimate routes:

1. File evidence from a command that actually executes every owned path — e.g. run vitest directly against tests/fault/foundation in addition to the package gate, and state both commands and both tails as evidence. The instruction-contract task set this precedent: it owned tests/instruction-contract/** and gated on `pnpm exec vitest run tests/instruction-contract`, unfiltered, precisely because a package filter cannot see tests/.

2. If you believe the task's declared Verification line must change, say so in #architects before proceeding rather than silently substituting a different command. Changing a task's declared gate is a task-definition decision.

Do not narrow the owned paths to fit the command. The tests are real coverage and dropping them to make the gate honest would be the wrong repair.

General lesson, recorded here because it will recur: any task owning paths under tests/** cannot verify with a `pnpm --filter <pkg>` command. Package filters are scoped to that package's directory. Check that your declared gate's glob actually covers every owned path before filing evidence — a green exit code proves only that whatever ran, passed.
